## Samsung and SK Hynix to announce major chip supply deals with US tech firms at Korea-US AI summit

Deals of this scale would lock in multi-year HBM and DRAM supply for US hyperscalers and NVIDIA, structurally tightening the memory supply chain; any terms that favor SK Hynix over Samsung within the pact could sharpen the ongoing HBM competitive divergence between the two Korean giants.

- South Korean memory giants Samsung and SK Hynix are set to announce large-scale chip supply agreements with leading US technology companies, with the signing framed around a diplomatic AI summit.
- Most outlets cite approximately $950 billion as the deal total; one outlet references an $880 billion plan — the precise aggregate is not confirmed across all coverage.
- NVIDIA is named as one of the US counterparties in several headlines; other US buyers are not identified by name.
- The South Korean president traveled to Silicon Valley for the summit, embedding these commercial deals in a geopolitical and sovereign-AI alliance narrative.
- Seven-outlet coverage breadth indicates a coordinated announcement tied to the diplomatic event rather than a spontaneous leak.
